9.summary: Donald Trump claimed on Saturday aboard Air Force One that he personally asked Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum to stop sending oil to Cuba and that she complied. Sheinbaum denied this claim on Sunday, stating they never discussed oil shipments to Cuba in their conversations.
key_facts: Trump stated on Saturday: 'The president of Mexico, President Sheinbaum, was very good. I told her: Look, we don't want you to send oil there. And she is not sending anything.'
Sheinbaum responded on Sunday: 'We never spoke with President Trump about the oil issue with Cuba. The topic has not been touched on in any of the conversations.'
Trump signed an executive order on Thursday imposing tariffs on countries that supply oil to Cuba
Sheinbaum announced Mexico would send humanitarian aid to Cuba this week, including food assistance through the Navy
Sheinbaum instructed Foreign Minister Juan Ramón de la Fuente to contact U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to understand the scope of Trump's tariff order
9.leader_role: Sheinbaum denied Trump's claim that he asked her to stop oil shipments to Cuba, stated they never discussed this topic, warned the tariffs could cause a humanitarian crisis, instructed her foreign minister to contact the U.S. State Department for clarification, and announced Mexico would send humanitarian aid to Cuba while seeking diplomatic alternatives to continue oil support.

6.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum responded to U.S. President Donald Trump's executive order imposing tariffs on countries supplying oil to Cuba by stating Mexico would seek diplomatic solutions to avoid a humanitarian crisis while protecting Mexico from potential tariffs. She instructed Foreign Minister Juan Ramón de la Fuente to contact the U.S. State Department to understand the decree's scope and communicate concerns about humanitarian impacts on Cuba.
key_facts: Trump signed an executive order on January 30, 2026 imposing tariffs on countries supplying oil to Cuba
Cuba's Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez declared an 'international emergency' in response to the U.S. tariffs
In 2024, Mexico's Gasolinas de Bienestar exported 20,100 barrels per day of crude and 2,700 bpd of oil products to Cuba, equivalent to $600 million and representing 1% of Mexico's production
Venezuela has not sent crude or fuel to Cuba for about a month due to a U.S. blockade
Sheinbaum spoke with Trump on Thursday morning hours before the tariff announcement, but he did not mention the Cuba measures during their call
6.leader_role: Sheinbaum stated Mexico would seek diplomatic channels and alternatives to help Cuba while avoiding tariffs on Mexico, instructed her foreign minister to contact the U.S. State Department to understand the decree's scope, and emphasized Mexico's interest in preventing Cuban people from suffering a humanitarian crisis affecting hospitals, transportation and food access.

10.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum announced on Sunday that Mexico plans to send humanitarian aid to Cuba this week, including food and other essential supplies, coordinated through the Navy Ministry. Sheinbaum stated she did not discuss Cuban affairs in her phone conversation with U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday, while diplomatic efforts continue regarding oil shipments to Cuba.
key_facts: Sheinbaum announced the humanitarian aid shipment during a public event in Sonora state on Sunday
The aid will include food, household items, and basic supplies, delivered through Mexico's Navy Ministry
Trump told reporters he asked the Mexican president not to send oil to Cuba, but Sheinbaum denied discussing Cuban affairs with Trump
Mexican Foreign Minister Juan Ramón de la Fuente discussed the oil shipment issue with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio
Mexico became Cuba's main oil supplier after Venezuela suspended shipments following a U.S. military operation to remove President Nicolás Maduro
Pemex shipped nearly 20,000 barrels of oil per day to Cuba from January through September 30, 2025, which later fell to about 7,000 barrels by September
10.leader_role: Sheinbaum announced Mexico's plan to send humanitarian aid to Cuba this week while maintaining that diplomatic efforts continue to resolve oil shipment issues for humanitarian reasons. She explicitly denied discussing Cuban affairs with Trump and clarified that diplomatic communications occurred between her Foreign Minister and the U.S. Secretary of State.

0.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum sent a diplomatic letter to South Korean President Lee Jae-myung requesting assistance in arranging additional BTS concerts in Mexico due to overwhelming demand. Sheinbaum stated that approximately 1 million young people want tickets but only 150,000 are available for the three scheduled Mexico City concerts in May.
key_facts: Sheinbaum sent a diplomatic letter to South Korean President Lee Jae-myung requesting more BTS concerts in Mexico
According to Sheinbaum, around 1 million young people want tickets but only 150,000 are available
BTS has three concerts scheduled in Mexico City's GNP Seguros Stadium from May 7-10, 2025
The South Korean president responded that they are in contact with the promoter company and thanked Mexico for the interest
Mexico's consumer watchdog launched a probe into Ticketmaster and sanctioned resale platforms StubHub and Viagogo for 'abusive and disloyal practices'
Tickets were selling on Ticketmaster from 1,800 to 17,800 pesos, but resale platforms were charging 11,300 to 92,100 pesos
0.leader_role: Sheinbaum sent a formal diplomatic letter to the South Korean president requesting help arranging more BTS concerts and announced this action at her daily morning press conference, stating 'Everyone wants to go' and providing specific figures about ticket demand versus availability.

7.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum acknowledged on January 27, 2025 that Mexico had halted oil shipments to Cuba, stating it was a "sovereign decision" not made under U.S. pressure. When asked directly whether she denied reports of the halted shipment, Sheinbaum responded "It is a sovereign decision and it is made in the moment when necessary."
key_facts: Bloomberg first reported the suspension of the oil shipment, with Reuters reporting that the Mexican government was reviewing whether to continue shipments amid fears of U.S. reprisals
Mexico was Cuba's second-largest oil supplier in 2025 with approximately 5,000 barrels per day, becoming critical after Venezuela stopped shipments about a month ago
Pemex exported 17,200 barrels per day of crude and 2,000 barrels per day of petroleum products to Cuba in the nine months ending September 2024
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited Mexico City in September 2025, after which oil shipments to Cuba reportedly fell from nearly 20,000 to about 7,000 barrels per day
7.leader_role: Sheinbaum confirmed the halt in oil shipments during her morning press conference, stating decisions were sovereign and not based on U.S. pressure. She sidestepped questions about resuming shipments, saying "in any case, it will be reported" and described oil decisions as either contractual through Pemex or humanitarian government decisions.
